name: sre

findings.message: When jq fails to update the verdict blob for a skipped (already-complete) cycle member, stderr is suppressed via `2>/dev/null` and the `&&` short-circuit leaves `blob` unchanged; cycle exit predicates (`exit_when`, `abort_when`, `until`) referencing that member then evaluate against a blob that is missing its entry, producing incorrect cycle-exit decisions with no machine-readable event and only a stderr warn that is easily lost in log volume.
findings.quote:
_cmbr_new_blob="$(jq -c --arg s "$s" --argjson e "$_cmbr_blob_entry" \
                    '. + {($s): $e}' <<< "$blob" 2>/dev/null)" \
                    && blob="$_cmbr_new_blob" \
                    || warn "cycle-orchestrator: failed to update verdict blob for skipped member '$s'; cycle predicates (exit_when/abort_when/until) may evaluate incorrectly"

findings.message: When `_cycle_state_write_iter_start` fails, only a stderr warn is printed and no machine-readable event is emitted; a subsequent interruption mid-iteration leaves `current_iter` at whatever value was last successfully written (the previously-completed iteration number), so a resume silently restarts from the wrong iteration, defeating RQLOOP-1 with no observable signal other than a potentially-missed stderr line.
findings.quote:
_cycle_state_write_iter_start "$state_file" "$cycle_id" "$iter" \
            || warn "cycle-orchestrator: failed to write iter-start state for cycle=$cycle_id iter=$iter (a resume may start at the wrong iteration)"

findings.message: When `_artifact_persist_put_back` fails mid-copy inside `_runner_resume_rehydrate`, the function returns 0 with only a stderr warn and no machine-readable event; artifacts already copied before the failure remain in `ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR` (partial restoration), so complete stages whose artifacts happened to have been copied before the failure are silently skipped by the dispatch-loop guard while only the first stage whose artifact is absent triggers the fail-closed `stage.verdict.stale_artifact` event — the root cause (put_back failure) is unobservable from event logs alone.
findings.quote:
_artifact_persist_put_back "$_rr_staging/artifacts" "$_rr_artifacts_dir" \
            || warn "resume-rehydrate: put_back failed for $_rr_artifacts_dir — partial restoration; dispatch loop will exit 1 for any missing primary artifact"

findings.message: When `_runner_from_stage_preflight` refuses a `--from-stage` run because a prior stage has no restorable artifact (DSFSTG-2 path), it emits only a stderr line before returning 1; unlike the dispatch-loop stale-artifact check at line 3935 which emits a `stage.verdict.stale_artifact` event before exiting, the preflight path emits no machine-readable event, so a monitoring system reading events.jsonl sees `pipeline.resume` then `pipeline.abort` with no distinguishable reason — it cannot tell a preflight validation refusal from a user-initiated abort.
findings.quote:
echo "error: --from-stage '$_fsp_from_stage': stage '$_fsp_s' has no restorable primary artifact" >&2
            return 1

reason: the sre lens found a medium or high or critical problem the change introduced
